title: Hamburg Steak
subtitle: Japanese hamburger steak with savoury soy sauce
excerpt: Hamburg steak is a Japanese comfort food classic: a juicy, oval beef and pork patty pan-fried until caramelised and served with a savoury soy and mirin sauce. It is the Japanese take on a Salisbury steak. Serves 4.
sourceNotes: Hamburg steak entered Japan in the Meiji period and was adapted into a beloved yoshoku home-cooking dish, lighter and more delicate than its Western counterpart.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze uncooked shaped patties between sheets of baking paper for up to 1 month. Cook from frozen over low heat with a lid.
recipe.batchNotes: Double the batch and freeze half the raw patties for another night.

glossaryTerms.definition: A category of Japanese cuisine that adapts Western dishes into a distinctly Japanese style, often with soy-based sauces and accompaniments.
Japanese-style breadcrumbs with a coarser, flakier texture than Western breadcrumbs. They keep meat patties moist and light when mixed into the mixture.

Mixing the meat mixture until slightly sticky is important. That tackiness binds the patty so it holds together when flipped.
Cook the diced onion in a little oil over medium heat for 5 minutes until soft and lightly golden. Spread on a plate and cool completely.
Combine both minces, cooled onion, panko, egg, and ginger in a bowl. Mix firmly with your hands for 2 minutes until the mixture is slightly sticky. Divide into 4 oval patties about 2 cm thick.

Heat oil in a large frying pan over high heat. Add the patties and sear for 3 minutes until deeply browned. Flip, reduce heat to medium, add 2 tablespoons of water, and cover with a lid. Steam for 7 minutes.
Remove the patties to a warm plate to rest for 5 minutes. Mix soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar, and sesame oil in a small bowl.
Pour off excess fat from the pan. Add the sauce mixture and bubble for 2 minutes over medium heat, stirring to pick up the meaty residue. Pour over the rested patties and serve with rice.

attrs.symptom: Patties puff up into a dome shape
attrs.cause: Steam builds up in the centre of the patty as it cooks.
attrs.fix: Press a small indent into the top of each raw patty before cooking. It flattens out as it cooks.

attrs.cause: The mixture was not mixed enough to bind or the patties are too cold to hold their shape.
attrs.fix: Mix the meat for a full 2 minutes until it feels tacky. Shape and refrigerate for 15 minutes before frying.

attrs.cause: The pan was not hot enough when the sauce was added.
attrs.fix: Bring the sauce to a vigorous bubble over medium-high heat and stir for 2 minutes until it coats a spoon.

content.text: Hamburg steak is yoshoku, Japan's tradition of adapting Western food into something entirely its own. The dish arrived in Japan in the Meiji era with German and British influences and was quickly claimed by home cooks. Today it is a school lunch staple and a go-to weeknight dinner. The soy-and-mirin sauce makes it unmistakably Japanese despite its European roots.
